title: Transport of finite-free coefficient maps between etale and pro-etale realizations
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ and a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Let $X,V,Z$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes, $f:V\to X$ separated of finite type, and $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ a closed immersion [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. On ordinary small etale derived categories use $Rf_{*,R}$, $G_R=Ri_R^!$ right adjoint to $i_{*,R}$, and $\omega_R=a_{X,R}^{\times}R$, where $a_X:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $a_{X,R}^{\times}$ is right adjoint to the compact-support functor defined by a fixed compactification [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, lem-exc-closed-ambient, def-amb-etale-compact-support, thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. Write $H_R(K,M)=R\mathcal Hom_R(K,M)$ and $D_RK=H_R(K,\omega_R)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom, lem-weil-duality-pairing].

Let $E\subset L$ be finite extensions of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, with ramification index $e$, and let $n\ge1$. Put $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ and $B=\mathcal O_L/\varpi_L^{en}=\mathcal O_L/\varpi_E^n\mathcal O_L$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], so $B$ is finite free over $A$. For each scheme $W$ use the site comparison $\nu_W:W_{\mathrm{proet}}\to W_{\mathrm{et}}$ and its exact derived pullback $C_W=\nu_W^*$ [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism, def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback]. Use bounded constructible finite-Tor inputs on the etale site [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes] and their pro-etale realizations [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility, def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. The pro-etale exceptional functor is the transported etale functor, with the transported adjunction counit [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. Use the canonical direct-image counit-mate site comparison, tensor pullback comparison, and evaluation-normalized internal-Hom and dualizing comparisons [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback, lem-weil-finite-duality-site-comparison]. For a coefficient map $a:R\to S$ put $T_a=-\otimes_R^LS$. Let $c_a:T_aRf_{*,R}\to Rf_{*,S}T_a$ be the extended inverse-image counit transpose; let $b_a:T_aG_R\to G_ST_a$ be the extended exceptional counit transpose using the inverse closed-direct-image comparison; and let $u_a:T_a\omega_R\to\omega_S$ be the extended structure-morphism compact-support counit transpose. The compact-support comparison is the proper projection comparison composed with open extension by zero. Let $v_a:T_aH_R(K,M)\to H_S(T_aK,T_aM)$ be the transpose of extended evaluation. Set $\beta_a=H_S(1,u_a)\circ v_{a;K,\omega_R}$ for Verdier duality. All these are the specified morphisms, with balanced tensor associators understood.

Under these specified endpoint identifications, the pullbacks $C$ of the etale maps $c,b,u,v,\beta$ are the corresponding pro-etale projection, exceptional-counit, dualizing-counit, evaluation, and Verdier maps. In particular this is equality of the named morphisms, not just existence of endpoint isomorphisms. Their evaluation, double-dual, counit and successive-extension identities are carried to the pro-etale realization. For $1\le m\le n$, the same conclusion holds for the quotient maps at $(n,m)$ over $E$ and $(en,em)$ over $L$. In the closed-exceptional case the etale quotient map is the exceptional-counit transpose specified above, and both outputs are bounded constructible finite-Tor by the closed case of [lem-coef-etale-locally-closed-shriek]; faithfulness of $C_Z$ on these bounded-below outputs [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] detects equality of their mixed reduction diagrams. Consequently the mixed reduction square formed on either site is carried to the named square on the other, and equality descends in the closed-exceptional case. No adjunction on the entire unbounded pro-etale category is asserted.

proof.text:
Write superscripts $e,p$ for the two sites, $C_{W,R}$ for comparison at coefficient $R$, and $T_W^e,T_W^p$ for extension along a fixed coefficient map $a:R\to S$. The scalar comparison
$$s_W:C_{W,S}T_W^e\xrightarrow{\sim}T_W^pC_{W,R}$$
is the inverse-image/scalar comparison of [lem-sfb-kflat-scalar-comparison-normalization]. Its scalar unit is fixed by $x\mapsto x\otimes1$. By [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons] it respects tensor reassociation, coefficient units and symmetry, and it respects composition of coefficient maps: view scalar change as pullback along the identity topos with its ring map, and use the commutation of this map with $\nu_W$. These are the canonical ringed commutation comparisons, since both are induced by the same balanced tensor map. No flatness of $a$ is used. For the finite-free horizontal extension, [lem-sf-finite-free-derived-scalar-calculus] gives preservation of bounded constructibility and the same Tor interval; for quotients use the bounded flat constructible model of [lem-sf-flat-model] and its reduction in [lem-sf-reduction-flat-model]. Each reduced term is constructible: on a stratum where that finite constructible term is constant it is the same constant finite module tensored with $S$. Finally [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude] gives the stated Tor bounds and constructibility after comparison.

source.place: Paragraphs 1-3, finite scalar extension and quotient/extension reassociation; Stacks 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product), 0D6D (lemma-derived-pullback-composition).

proof.text:
Put $d_{f,R}:C_{X,R}Rf^e_{*,R}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf^p_{*,R}C_{V,R}$. The hypotheses for [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate] hold: these separated finite-type morphisms between Noetherian finite-type $k$-schemes are quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and the inputs are bounded below. Use its counit-normalized $d$, not an arbitrary isomorphism. The direct-image assertion is the equation
$$d_{f,S;T^eK}\,C_{X,S}(c_a^e)=Rf^p_{*,S}(s_V^{-1})\,c_a^p\,T_X^p(d_{f,R;K})\,s_X.$$
Indeed apply the canonical $f_S^*\dashv Rf_{*,S}$ Hom bijection to both sides. Substituting the normalization $\varepsilon^p f_p^*(d)a_f=C(\varepsilon^e)$ makes the left transpose the $S$-extension of $C_{V,R}(\varepsilon^e_{f,K})$; the right transpose is exactly the same map, because $s$ commutes with pullback composition and tensor units. Formally this is the pasting equation of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting], with scalar change as an identity-topos ringed edge and the site square as the other edge. The adjunction bijection is injective, hence the displayed equality holds for the named coefficient counit transpose. For arbitrary finite $a$ its inverse is available on these inputs by [lem-coef-finite-direct-image].

source.place: Paragraph 1, ordinary direct-image comparison; Stacks categories.tex 0B65 (lemma-transformation-between-functors-and-adjoints), sites-cohomology.tex 0E48 (remark-compatible-with-diagram).

proof.text: The compact-support coefficient comparison $c_a^{!,e}$ is the proper direct-image comparison followed by the open scalar comparison, at the fixed compactification. The latter is [lem-coef-etale-open-tensor] on the etale site and [lem-fix-open-scalar-tensor-normalization] on the pro-etale site. The site comparison $B_{f,R}:C_YF^e_{f,R}\xrightarrow{\sim}F^p_{f,R}C_X$ is the specified proper/open composite in [lem-pur-compact-support-site-coherence]. Apply step 2 to the proper part. For the open part compare the two resulting $S$-linear maps $C_ST^ej_!^eP\to j_!^pT^pC_RP$. The scalar/open maps on both sites are open-adjunction transposes of the identity on the open, as specified in the two open-scalar nodes. The site/open map is the specified adjoint comparison in $B_f$. Paste these open and scalar adjunction squares by [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting]; both resulting transposes are the same identity after the scalar/site pullback identification $s_U$. Therefore they are equal in the $S$-coefficient category itself. Under scalar restriction this is also exactly [lem-sf-comparison-open-tensor-coherence] at the constant module $S$. Compose with the proper equality to obtain step 2's square for $F_f,c_a^!$, with $d$ replaced by $B_f$. For $i$ use its identity-open compactification: [lem-coef-proper-identity-open-site-comparison] identifies its $B_i$ with the named closed direct-image mate, including identity extension by zero. Thus the coefficient and site comparisons in its inverse have precisely the closed normalization used to define $b_a$.

source.place: Paragraph 1, compact-support comparison used to transpose the dualizing counit; Stacks 0GL1 (lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor).

proof.text:
Let $F_R=i_{*,R}$ or $F_R=Ra_{X,R!}$, and let $G_R$ be its etale right adjoint. Write $\rho_R:CG_R\xrightarrow{\sim}G_R^pC$ for the transported comparison. All transposes below have bounded-below inputs: [lem-coef-etale-locally-closed-shriek] with the open immersion equal to the identity and the identity quotient gives $G_RM$ bounded constructible finite-Tor on the etale site; [lem-weil-verdier-preservation-strata] applied to the coefficient unit gives the same typing for $\omega_R$: the unit is bounded constructible of Tor amplitude $[0,0]$, and $D_R(R)=H_R(R,\omega_R)=\omega_R$. This works at every $E$- and $L$-stage. A finite-dimensional chosen compactification exists here; its dimension is finite by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type]. Thus [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] and [lem-pur-bounded-site-adjunction-transpose] apply with the same compactification and give
$$\varepsilon_R^p F_R^p(\rho_R)B_R=C(\varepsilon_R^e).$$
Apply the latter node's transpose assertion at coefficient $S$ to
$$F_S^eT^eG_RM\xrightarrow{(c_a^{!,e})^{-1}}T^eF_R^eG_RM\xrightarrow{T^e\varepsilon_R^e}T^eM.$$
Step 3 identifies the pulled-forward first arrow with the inverse pro-etale coefficient comparison; the displayed equation identifies the second with the pro-etale counit. Its transpose is therefore precisely $b_a^p$ for $i$, or the structure-morphism transpose for $a_X$. Under $s$ and $\rho$ it is $C(b_a^e)$, respectively $C(u_a^e)$. At $a_X$ evaluate on the coefficient unit $R$ and use $T_aR=S$. The dualizing endpoint is the specified one of [lem-weil-finite-duality-site-comparison]. Only the bounded-below etale-origin adjunction is used.

source.place: Paragraph 1, exceptional and structure-morphism counit transposes; Stacks categories.tex 0B65 (lemma-transformation-between-functors-and-adjoints).

proof.text:
For the Hom assertion put $r_R:CH_R(K,M)\xrightarrow{\sim}H_R(CK,CM)$, the evaluation-defined comparison of [lem-weil-finite-duality-site-comparison]. Write $\bar v^e$ for $C(v_a^e)$ with all scalar and input comparisons inserted, so that its source is $T^pCH_R(K,M)$ and target is $CH_S(T^eK,T^eM)$. We claim
$$r_S\bar v^e=v_a^p\,T^p(r_R).$$
Use the tensor--Hom bijection in [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal] with first tensor factor the common source and second factor $C_ST^eK$. On the left, the defining evaluation equation for $r_S$ and then that for $v_a^e$ give $C_ST^e(\mathrm{ev}_R)$ after the canonical tensor identifications. On the right, the defining equation for $v_a^p$ gives $T^p(\mathrm{ev}_R^p)\circ(T^p r_R\otimes1)$, which is the same $C_ST^e(\mathrm{ev}_R)$ by the defining equation for $r_R$ and naturality of $s$. The tensor identifications agree by the monoidal composition equations of step 1. Injectivity of the Hom bijection proves the claim. This calculation proves equality of the evaluation-normalized morphisms, including when $a$ is a quotient. Its use of $r_S$ is legitimate: the scalar-changed inputs remain bounded constructible finite-Tor by step 1.

source.place: Paragraph 2, internal-Hom comparison is adjoint to the same evaluation; Stacks 08J9 (lemma-internal-hom).

proof.text: The Verdier map is the composite $H_S(1,u_a)\circ v_{a;K,\omega_R}$. Naturality of $r_S$ in its second variable, step 4 for $u_a$, and step 5 for $v_a$ therefore identify $C(\beta_a^e)$ with the named pro-etale composite. This is substitution into the specified formula, with no new comparison chosen. The evaluation and double-dual equations are carried along these same identifications: [lem-weil-finite-duality-site-comparison] identifies both the pairing and its specified transpose; [lem-weil-duality-pairing] defines the double-dual arrow by evaluation with the tensor symmetry. Step 1 preserves that symmetry, so transposing gives the same double-dual arrow after transport. This argument does not require assuming biduality on an ambient category.

source.place: Paragraphs 2-3, Verdier comparison, evaluation and double-dual compatibility.

proof.text: For successive finite-free coefficient maps, [lem-sf-finite-free-comparison-transitivity] gives the etale equations for all five named maps. Apply $C$ to each equality and use steps 2-6 for its individual arrows. The scalar composition comparison of step 1 identifies the transported tensor reassociation with the canonical pro-etale reassociation, so the resulting equations are exactly the pro-etale successive-extension equations (including the identity case). Likewise apply $C$ to the defining etale counit identities: steps 2 and 4 identify the counits, step 3 the compact-support comparisons, hence the resulting equations are the named pro-etale counit identities. Functoriality preserves equality and composition; no inference from isomorphic endpoints is being used.

source.place: Paragraph 3, two field extensions and equality of counit/evaluation transposes.

proof.text: Now take $q_A:A_{E,n}\to A_{E,m}$ and $q_B:A_{L,en}\to A_{L,em}$, with $1\le m\le n$. Steps 1-5 used derived scalar extension and did not assume flatness of these vertical maps. The quotient direct-image and Hom morphisms in [lem-coef-finite-direct-image] and [thm-coef-finite-hom] are exactly the inverse-image-counit and evaluation transposes specified in the item. The dualizing quotient morphism is the structure-morphism compact-support counit transpose already treated in step 4; it needs no downstream coefficient theorem. For the closed exceptional arrow apply [lem-coef-etale-locally-closed-shriek] with the open immersion equal to the identity. It gives $G_RM$ finite-Tor bounded constructible and identifies the quotient arrow with the transpose of $T\varepsilon_R\circ c^{-1}$. Step 1 types $TG_RM$ and $TM$; apply the same closed lemma at the identity quotient over $S$ to type $G_STM$. Step 4 therefore transports precisely this quotient arrow to the specified pro-etale counit transpose. The dualizing and dual inputs are typed by [lem-weil-verdier-preservation-strata] at each of the four stages: apply it to the unit for $\omega_R$ and to the inputs for their duals. Their quotient reductions are typed by [lem-coef-finite-hom-domain-calculus] at $(n,m)$ over $E$ and $(en,em)$ over $L$. Thus steps 4-6 apply to all five vertical arrows and their evaluations, within the bounded etale-origin adjunction.

source.place: Paragraph 3, quotient followed by extension; closed-exceptional etale recovery and dual-input typing.

proof.text: Choose one $\mathcal O_E$-basis of $\mathcal O_L$ by [lem-sfb-local-field-integral-basis]; its reductions give compatible free bases at $n$ and $m$. The ring maps satisfy $q_Ba_n=a_mq_A$ on every element of $\mathcal O_E$. Apply the scalar pullback-composition comparison of [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons] to these two factorizations: both $R_BT_n$ and $T_mR_A$ identify with $-\otimes^L_{A_n}B_m$. On K-flat representatives the balancing maps are $((p\otimes a)\otimes b)\mapsto p\otimes ab$ and $((p\otimes b_n)\otimes b_m)\mapsto p\otimes q_B(b_n)b_m$. Also $B_n\otimes^L_{A_n}A_m=B_n\otimes_{A_n}A_m=B_m$, since $B_n$ is free and quotienting by $\varpi_E^m$ gives $B_m$. Step 1 identifies their images under $C$ with these same balanced maps. For any of the five mixed squares, apply $C$ to its two composites; steps 2-8 identify each of the four arrows with the corresponding named arrow on the pro-etale site. Functoriality then identifies the two whole diagrams, including their tensor reassociation edges. For the closed exceptional square step 8 and [lem-coef-etale-locally-closed-shriek] place the endpoints in the bounded-below etale category, so the full faithfulness of [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] implies that its two etale composites are equal if and only if their pullbacks are equal. This proves the claimed descent of equality. The indices are $(n,m)$ and $(en,em)$ throughout, never equal numerical indices for different uniformizers. The cases $m=n$, $E=L$, zero inputs and empty schemes reduce to identity maps or maps of zero objects in these same formulas.
